item.title: ‘Expect new dynamics’: Ukraine hopes for more support after Democrats sweep midterms
item.description: Ukraine anticipates enhanced military and financial assistance from the United States after the midterm elections. Foreign minister Andrii Sybiha expressed hope for new dynamics and support from the incoming Democratic majority. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy acknowledged the Democrats' vocal backing of Ukraine since their election success. This shift in power could enable legislation favoring aid to Ukraine despite previous limitations.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Montana Supreme Court awards husband $955,000 home despite property being in wife's name
item.description: In a contentious property dispute in Montana, a couple found themselves at odds after their marriage dissolved. The husband poured approximately $955,000 into their shared home, though it was registered solely in the wife's name. Ultimately, the Montana Supreme Court favored the husband, underscoring the significance of financial contributions over title ownership in divorce settlements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Backyard Railway Village: Chicago family turns garden into miniature town; hobby draws visitors
item.description: Over two decades, a Chicago family's backyard has transformed into a vibrant miniature railway town. What began as a modest garden endeavor blossomed into a captivating landscape filled with elaborate buildings and model trains. Despite initial worries about sacrificing garden space, family members embraced the hobby, turning their yard into a destination for train enthusiasts, while inspiring younger generations to explore the joys of model railroading.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Wife smears faeces in husband's mouth after threatening to make him eat it; gets suspended jail term
item.description: A 63-year-old woman in the UK has received a suspended prison sentence after smearing faeces into her husband's mouth during an argument at their £1 million farmhouse. Alison Moore had threatened to make him eat it before carrying out the attack. The judge described the act as a 'gratuitous degradation' of the victim.

item.title: Arkansas man loses challenge to sale of ex-wife's share of their jointly owned land
item.description: A couple bought land together in Arkansas in 2021 but divorced within a year, retaining equal ownership. After the woman filed for bankruptcy in 2023, a trustee sold her share to an investment company. Her former husband challenged the sale, but the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit dismissed his appeal because he had not challenged the buyer's good faith before the bankruptcy court.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kim Kardashian’s former mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed, listed for $8.5 million after makeover
item.description: Kim Kardashian’s former Beverly Hills mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed to her on camera in 2011, is heading to the market for nearly $8.5 million after an extensive makeover. Kim bought the property for $3.4 million in 2010 and sold it for $3.6 million in 2013. The five-bedroom estate now boasts luxurious modern interiors.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Louisiana court upholds a trust protector's powers to change beneficiaries and approve early closure
item.description: A Louisiana appeals court upheld a trust protector's authority to change future beneficiaries and require approval before a trust could be ended early. The case involved a trust created by a stepfather for his stepson in 2004. The stepson challenged the powers given to his stepbrother, but the court upheld the lower court's decision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Washington court broadens rules on divorce legal fees
item.description: Washington's Court of Appeals ruled that trial courts can award legal fees despite prenuptial agreements. This decision allows judges to consider broader divorce aspects for fee awards. In the case reviewed, a wealthy husband was ordered to pay his wife's legal costs. The trial court is to reassess the specific fee awards granted to the wife.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Once homeless himself, he is on a mission to end food insecurity
item.description: Dion Dawson founded Dion's Chicago Dream in 2020 to provide fresh produce to families facing food insecurity. After experiencing homelessness and food scarcity, he aimed to improve food distribution methods. The non-profit now delivers 80,000 pounds of fresh produce weekly to over 5,400 households. Paid staff members maintain a steady workforce while providing dignity to recipients through efficient service.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: He survived Hiroshima, returned home to Nagasaki and was hit by a second atomic bomb three days later: The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi
item.description: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a survivor of both atomic bombings, faced immense physical and emotional trauma from his experiences. Initially reluctant to share his story, he eventually became an advocate for a world free of nuclear weapons. His journey from hibakusha to spokesperson illustrates the lasting impact of nuclear warfare on individuals and communities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy and Zohran Mamdani: A tale of two Indian-Americans
item.description: Dickens wrote of the spring of hope and the winter of despair as two seasons belonging to the same age. The American electorate witnessed both in November 2026. Mamdani chose hope. Ramaswamy chose despair. And the results suggested which had proved more persuasive.

item.title: UK’s Burnham won’t invite Putin to G20 summit next year; he skips them anyway
item.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham confirmed that Vladimir Putin would not be invited to the 2027 G20 summit. This comes amid the intensified Russia-Ukraine war. However, the US has invited Putin to this year's G20, which has drawn criticism from European leaders. Russia continues to attend G20 meetings, though Putin doesn't attend in person.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: How Rory McIlroy’s £1 million gift helped Daisy Lodge
item.description: Rory McIlroy donated £1 million to establish Daisy Lodge, a center for families with children suffering from cancer. Since its opening in 2014, over 4,000 families have benefited from therapeutic short breaks at the lodge. The center provides support through workshops and complementary therapies while creating a space for families to connect. Tragically, some families have also received bereavement support following the loss of loved ones.
